Decode runs on trtllm-gen's FP8 kernel, as `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` does, and the grouped prefill of #63104 reads a BF16 copy of each prefill request's KV. Stacked on #63104, which depends on vllm-project/flash-attention#205: only the last commit is new. Default backend selection does not change. For a quantized cache the SM100 sparse priority list stays `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, so this path is opt-in with `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE_FA4`. Related work: LiteDSA (arXiv 2607.11976) groups neighbouring queries in the same way for the FP8 sparse MLA path, on a vendored FlashMLA SM100 FP8 kernel. It was proposed in #48726 and removed from it in a later commit, so #48726 now carries only the LiteTopk indexer. This PR instead dequantizes into #63104's BF16 path and FA4's existing kernel. The idea itself is not new (see #63104). #60806 (draft) would let the FA4 masked-MHA prefill serve an FP8 cache when the prefill query is BF16; prefills it routes to masked MHA would not reach this path, as with a BF16 cache in #63104. ## Claims - **`FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE_FA4` with an FP8 cache prefills 1.09-1.17x faster than the default FP8 backend** (`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`) on `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` (TP4, B300). With a quantized cache masked MHA is off, so this covers every sparse prefill. - **No measurable accuracy change:** GSM8K 5-shot exact match (strict / flexible) is 0.9363 / 0.9378 on the baseline and 0.9371 / 0.9393 with this PR (± 0.0067). On the same FP8 values, the grouped path's error against an fp32 reference is 3-9x lower (max) than trtllm-gen's FP8 kernel, because P·V stays in BF16. - BF16 behaviour and default backend selection are unchanged. ## Validation All runs: B300, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (8e2beaa3b), with this branch's three changed Python files and the three changed `cute` files of flash-attention#205 bind-mounted, as in #63104. I did not build this branch from source. **Tests** ```bash pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k 'query_group or fa4 or sparse_backend_decode_correctness' # 399 passed, 1350 skipped, 151 deselected in 1290s ``` `test_fa4_sparse_grouped_prefill_fp8_kv_cache[16, 32, 64 heads]` builds the FP8 cache and the packed FP8 query the DSA model passes, with q/k scales of 0.5/0.25. It runs a decode request and two prefills with tails through two layers of one index group. Dropping either the query or the cache scale fails all three cases; I checked both. **End-to-end prefill latency**, FP8 cache on both servers: baseline nightly with its default backend on GPUs 0-3, this PR with `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE_FA4` on GPUs 4-7. The flags are otherwise those of #63104, with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, and the script is `e2e_prefill.py` from #63104. The unit test's inputs, with more tokens, give 352 / 176 / 90 grouped rows. Errors are against fp32 attention on the same dequantized FP8 query and cache. The larger softmax scale peaks the attention. | Heads per rank | Softmax scale | Grouped FA4 on the BF16 copy, max / mean | trtllm-gen FP8, max / mean | |---|---|---|---| | 16 | 1/sqrt(576) | 0.0003 / 0.00003 | 0.0027 / 0.00039 | | 16 | 16/sqrt(576) | 0.0015 / 0.00008 | 0.0050 / 0.00067 | | 32 | 1/sqrt(576) | 0.0003 / 0.00003 | 0.0024 / 0.00038 | | 32 | 16/sqrt(576) | 0.0015 / 0.00007 | 0.0048 / 0.00067 | | 64 | 1/sqrt(576) | 0.0003 / 0.00003 | 0.0027 / 0.00038 | | 64 | 16/sqrt(576) | 0.0017 / 0.00008 | 0.0051 / 0.00066 | **Cost of the two extra steps**, per layer and prefill request on a B300 (`bench_staging.py`, `bench_qdequant.py`), each the median of 50 calls: | Request tokens | 8K | 16K | 32K | 48K | |---|---|---|---|---| | Stage the cache rows to BF16 (`gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache`) | 18 us | 19 us | 21 us | 25 us | | Dequantize the 16-head FP8 query (Triton) | 54 us | | | 216 us | | ... with torch's `.to(torch.bfloat16)` instead | 213 us | | | 1,216 us |

Reuses the unit test's inputs; run from a vLLM checkout inside the nightly image.""" import torch import tests.v1.attention.test_sparse_mla_backends as T from vllm.platforms import current_platform from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla import flashattn_mla_sparse as M from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.index_group import SparseMLAIndexGroupBuilder from vllm.v1.worker.workspace import WorkspaceManager workspace = WorkspaceManager(torch.device("cuda")) M.current_workspace_manager = lambda: workspace q_scale, k_scale = 0.5, 0.25 fp8 = current_platform.fp8_dtype() for num_heads in (16, 32, 64): group = 128 // num_heads query_lens = [1, 24 * group + 3, 20 * group + 1] inputs = T._fa4_prefill_inputs(num_heads, query_lens, [300, 700, 650], device="cuda") q = (torch.cat(inputs.q, dim=-1).float() / q_scale).to(fp8) kv_cache = (inputs.kv_cache.float() / k_scale).to(fp8) layer = T.SimpleNamespace(_q_scale_float=q_scale, _k_scale_float=k_scale, _k_scale=torch.tensor(k_scale, device="cuda")) grouped = torch.zeros(sum(query_lens), dtype=torch.bool, device="cuda") first = query_lens[0] for n in query_lens[1:]: grouped[first: first + n // group * group] = True first += n for peak in (1, 16): inputs.scale = (576 ** -0.5) * peak reference = T._fa4_prefill_reference(inputs, q.float() * q_scale, kv_cache.float() * k_scale)[grouped] row = {} for name, spans in (("grouped FA4 (BF16 copy)", None), ("trtllm-gen FP8", lambda *a, **k: None)): impl = T._fa4_impl(inputs.logical, scale=inputs.scale, kv_cache_dtype="fp8", staged_kv_shape=(1024, 576), index_group=SparseMLAIndexGroupBuilder(inputs.logical).register_layer(True)[0]) if spans is not None: impl._query_group_spans = spans M.FlashAttnMLASparseFA4Impl._query_group_unions = None with torch.inference_mode(): out = impl.forward_mqa(q, kv_cache, inputs.metadata, layer)[0].float()[grouped] err = (out - reference).abs() row[name] = f"max {err.max():.4f} mean {err.mean():.5f}" print(f"heads {num_heads:2d} | softmax scale x{peak:2d} | {grouped.sum().item()} rows | " + " | ".join(f"{k}: {v}" for k, v in row.items()), flush=True) ``` ```python """Cost of the FP8 path's two extra steps for one prefill request of S tokens on one layer: staging the request's S cache rows to BF16 (gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache) and dequantizing its packed FP8 query (16 heads x 576). Median of 50 CUDA-event-timed calls.""" import torch from vllm import _custom_ops as ops from vllm.utils.math_utils import cdiv BLOCK, WIDTH, HEADS, LAYERS = 64, 576, 16, 78 def timed(fn) -> float: fn() times = [] for _ in range(50): start, end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) start.record(); fn(); end.record(); torch.cuda.synchronize() times.append(start.elapsed_time(end) * 1e3) return sorted(times)[len(times) // 2] for seq_len in (8192, 16384, 32768, 49152): blocks = cdiv(seq_len, BLOCK) cache = torch.randint(0, 120, (blocks + 256, BLOCK, WIDTH), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda") block_table = torch.randperm(blocks + 256, device="cuda")[:blocks].to(torch.int32)[None] bounds = torch.tensor([0, seq_len], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") token_to_seq = torch.zeros(seq_len, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") staged = torch.empty(65536, WIDTH, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") scale = torch.tensor(1.0, device="cuda") stage = timed(lambda: ops.gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache( cache.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn), staged, block_table, bounds, token_to_seq, seq_len, "fp8", scale)) q = torch.randint(0, 120, (seq_len, HEADS, WIDTH), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda").view(torch.float8_e4m3fn) dequant = timed(lambda: q.to(torch.bfloat16).mul_(0.5)) print(f"S={seq_len:6d}: stage {stage:6.1f} us, query dequant {dequant:6.1f} us per layer | " f"x{LAYERS} layers {(stage + dequant) * LAYERS / 1e3:5.2f} ms per forward") ``` ```python """Ways to turn the packed FP8 query (S x 16 heads x 576) into BF16: torch cast, torch cast + scale, and a Triton dequant kernel. Median of 50 CUDA-event-timed calls.""" import torch from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton @triton.jit def _dequant_kernel(src, dst, scale, n, BLOCK: tl.constexpr): offs = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK) x = tl.load(src + offs, offs < n) tl.store(dst + offs, (x.to(tl.float32) * scale).to(tl.bfloat16), offs < n) def triton_dequant(q, scale): out = torch.empty(q.shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=q.device) n = q.numel() _dequant_kernel[(triton.cdiv(n, 4096),)](q, out, scale, n, BLOCK=4096) return out def timed(fn) -> float: fn() times = [] for _ in range(50): start, end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) start.record(); fn(); end.record(); torch.cuda.synchronize() times.append(start.elapsed_time(end) * 1e3) return sorted(times)[len(times) // 2] for seq_len in (8192, 49152): q = torch.randint(0, 120, (seq_len, 16, 576), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda").view(torch.float8_e4m3fn) ref = q.to(torch.bfloat16).mul_(0.5) assert torch.equal(triton_dequant(q, 0.5), ref) print(f"S={seq_len:6d}: cast {timed(lambda: q.to(torch.bfloat16)):7.1f} us | " f"cast+mul {timed(lambda: q.to(torch.bfloat16).mul_(0.5)):7.1f} us | " f"triton {timed(lambda: triton_dequant(q, 0.5)):7.1f} us | " f"bytes moved {q.numel() * 3 / 1e6:.0f} MB") ```
## Details **Why.** FA4's MLA kernel takes no descales, so with an FP8 cache the FA4 backend accepted only BF16 and FP8 deployments could not use the grouped prefill. **Changes** - `FlashAttnMLASparseFA4Backend` lists `fp8` and `fp8_e4m3`. With a quantized cache the impl: - decodes through the trtllm-gen path it inherits (its LSE converted to base e, as for trtllm-gen prefill); - runs decode rows, per-request tails and padding rows of a grouped batch on trtllm-gen too; - for each prefill request, copies its rows `[0, seq_len)` to BF16 with `ops.gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache` into a workspace of `max_model_len x 576`. The workspace is reserved at init through the workspace manager, as FlashMLA's prefill workspace is. - The union then maps positions to themselves (an identity block table), so the 2^24 row limit applies to positions rather than cache rows. - The packed FP8 query of the grouped rows is dequantized with a small Triton kernel, `sparse_utils.dequantize_fp8`. Torch's FP8 cast reached about 1 TB/s here. - The layer still quantizes the query (`supports_quant_query_input` is unchanged), so decode is exactly the FlashInfer path. **Using it.** Pass `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE_FA4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` (or `fp8`). - Grouping needs 16, 32 or 64 query heads per rank: GLM-5.x at TP4, TP2 or TP1, and DeepSeek-V3.2 at TP8, TP4 or TP2. Otherwise prefill silently stays on trtllm-gen; GLM-5.x at TP8 is one such case. - With NIXL P/D disaggregation, both sides must run the same attention backend, because NIXL's compatibility hash includes it. With an FP8 cache FA4 decodes on trtllm-gen, so a decode instance on this backend decodes as `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` does. **Tradeoffs and limitations** - **Smaller gain than with BF16 KV (1.4-1.5x in #63104).** The baseline gets much faster with an FP8 cache: its 48K prefill takes 1.89 s instead of 2.60 s with BF16, trtllm-gen in both cases. This path stays near 1.72 s because it computes in BF16. A native FP8 grouped kernel, as in #48726, would keep FP8's advantage. - **Memory.** The workspace is `max_model_len x 1,152 B` (75 MB at 64K). The dequantized query is a temporary of `tokens x heads x 1,152 B` per request, the same size as the head-major query copy of #63104's BF16 path. - **Query precision.** Grouped rows use the FP8 query the layer already produced for trtllm-gen, dequantized. Keeping a BF16 query for them would need the layer to quantize only the rows trtllm-gen reads. AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change, its tests and the benchmarks, which ran on my machine; I reviewed every changed line. This stays a draft until #63104 and flash-attention#205 are merged. ---

(Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

Reuses the unit test's inputs; run from a vLLM checkout inside the nightly image.""" import torch import tests.v1.attention.test_sparse_mla_backends as T from vllm.platforms import current_platform from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla import flashattn_mla_sparse as M from vllm.v1.attention.backends.mla.index_group import SparseMLAIndexGroupBuilder from vllm.v1.worker.workspace import WorkspaceManager workspace = WorkspaceManager(torch.device("cuda")) M.current_workspace_manager = lambda: workspace q_scale, k_scale = 0.5, 0.25 fp8 = current_platform.fp8_dtype() for num_heads in (16, 32, 64): group = 128 // num_heads query_lens = [1, 24 * group + 3, 20 * group + 1] inputs = T._fa4_prefill_inputs(num_heads, query_lens, [300, 700, 650], device="cuda") q = (torch.cat(inputs.q, dim=-1).float() / q_scale).to(fp8) kv_cache = (inputs.kv_cache.float() / k_scale).to(fp8) layer = T.SimpleNamespace(_q_scale_float=q_scale, _k_scale_float=k_scale, _k_scale=torch.tensor(k_scale, device="cuda")) grouped = torch.zeros(sum(query_lens), dtype=torch.bool, device="cuda") first = query_lens[0] for n in query_lens[1:]: grouped[first: first + n // group * group] = True first += n for peak in (1, 16): inputs.scale = (576 ** -0.5) * peak reference = T._fa4_prefill_reference(inputs, q.float() * q_scale, kv_cache.float() * k_scale)[grouped] row = {} for name, spans in (("grouped FA4 (BF16 copy)", None), ("trtllm-gen FP8", lambda *a, **k: None)): impl = T._fa4_impl(inputs.logical, scale=inputs.scale, kv_cache_dtype="fp8", staged_kv_shape=(1024, 576), index_group=SparseMLAIndexGroupBuilder(inputs.logical).register_layer(True)[0]) if spans is not None: impl._query_group_spans = spans M.FlashAttnMLASparseFA4Impl._query_group_unions = None with torch.inference_mode(): out = impl.forward_mqa(q, kv_cache, inputs.metadata, layer)[0].float()[grouped] err = (out - reference).abs() row[name] = f"max {err.max():.4f} mean {err.mean():.5f}" print(f"heads {num_heads:2d} | softmax scale x{peak:2d} | {grouped.sum().item()} rows | " + " | ".join(f"{k}: {v}" for k, v in row.items()), flush=True) ``` ```python """Cost of the FP8 path's two extra steps for one prefill request of S tokens on one layer: staging the request's S cache rows to BF16 (gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache) and dequantizing its packed FP8 query (16 heads x 576). Median of 50 CUDA-event-timed calls.""" import torch from vllm import _custom_ops as ops from vllm.utils.math_utils import cdiv BLOCK, WIDTH, HEADS, LAYERS = 64, 576, 16, 78 def timed(fn) -> float: fn() times = [] for _ in range(50): start, end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) start.record(); fn(); end.record(); torch.cuda.synchronize() times.append(start.elapsed_time(end) * 1e3) return sorted(times)[len(times) // 2] for seq_len in (8192, 16384, 32768, 49152): blocks = cdiv(seq_len, BLOCK) cache = torch.randint(0, 120, (blocks + 256, BLOCK, WIDTH), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda") block_table = torch.randperm(blocks + 256, device="cuda")[:blocks].to(torch.int32)[None] bounds = torch.tensor([0, seq_len], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") token_to_seq = torch.zeros(seq_len, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") staged = torch.empty(65536, WIDTH, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") scale = torch.tensor(1.0, device="cuda") stage = timed(lambda: ops.gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache( cache.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn), staged, block_table, bounds, token_to_seq, seq_len, "fp8", scale)) q = torch.randint(0, 120, (seq_len, HEADS, WIDTH), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda").view(torch.float8_e4m3fn) dequant = timed(lambda: q.to(torch.bfloat16).mul_(0.5)) print(f"S={seq_len:6d}: stage {stage:6.1f} us, query dequant {dequant:6.1f} us per layer | " f"x{LAYERS} layers {(stage + dequant) * LAYERS / 1e3:5.2f} ms per forward") ``` ```python """Ways to turn the packed FP8 query (S x 16 heads x 576) into BF16: torch cast, torch cast + scale, and a Triton dequant kernel. Median of 50 CUDA-event-timed calls.""" import torch from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton @triton.jit def _dequant_kernel(src, dst, scale, n, BLOCK: tl.constexpr): offs = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK) x = tl.load(src + offs, offs < n) tl.store(dst + offs, (x.to(tl.float32) * scale).to(tl.bfloat16), offs < n) def triton_dequant(q, scale): out = torch.empty(q.shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=q.device) n = q.numel() _dequant_kernel[(triton.cdiv(n, 4096),)](q, out, scale, n, BLOCK=4096) return out def timed(fn) -> float: fn() times = [] for _ in range(50): start, end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) start.record(); fn(); end.record(); torch.cuda.synchronize() times.append(start.elapsed_time(end) * 1e3) return sorted(times)[len(times) // 2] for seq_len in (8192, 49152): q = torch.randint(0, 120, (seq_len, 16, 576), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda").view(torch.float8_e4m3fn) ref = q.to(torch.bfloat16).mul_(0.5) assert torch.equal(triton_dequant(q, 0.5), ref) print(f"S={seq_len:6d}: cast {timed(lambda: q.to(torch.bfloat16)):7.1f} us | " f"cast+mul {timed(lambda: q.to(torch.bfloat16).mul_(0.5)):7.1f} us | " f"triton {timed(lambda: triton_dequant(q, 0.5)):7.1f} us | " f"bytes moved {q.numel() * 3 / 1e6:.0f} MB") ```
## Details **Why.** FA4's MLA kernel takes no descales, so with an FP8 cache the FA4 backend accepted only BF16 and FP8 deployments could not use the grouped prefill. **Changes** - `FlashAttnMLASparseFA4Backend` lists `fp8` and `fp8_e4m3`. With a quantized cache the impl: - decodes through the trtllm-gen path it inherits (its LSE converted to base e, as for trtllm-gen prefill); - runs decode rows, per-request tails and padding rows of a grouped batch on trtllm-gen too; - for each prefill request, copies its rows `[0, seq_len)` to BF16 with `ops.gather_and_maybe_dequant_cache` into a workspace of `max_model_len x 576`. The workspace is reserved at init through the workspace manager, as FlashMLA's prefill workspace is. - The union then maps positions to themselves (an identity block table), so the 2^24 row limit applies to positions rather than cache rows. - The packed FP8 query of the grouped rows is dequantized with a small Triton kernel, `sparse_utils.dequantize_fp8`. Torch's FP8 cast reached about 1 TB/s here. - The layer still quantizes the query (`supports_quant_query_input` is unchanged), so decode is exactly the FlashInfer path. **Using it.** Pass `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE_FA4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` (or `fp8`). - Grouping needs 16, 32 or 64 query heads per rank: GLM-5.x at TP4, TP2 or TP1, and DeepSeek-V3.2 at TP8, TP4 or TP2. Otherwise prefill silently stays on trtllm-gen; GLM-5.x at TP8 is one such case. - With NIXL P/D disaggregation, both sides must run the same attention backend, because NIXL's compatibility hash includes it. With an FP8 cache FA4 decodes on trtllm-gen, so a decode instance on this backend decodes as `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` does. **Tradeoffs and limitations** - **Smaller gain than with BF16 KV (1.4-1.5x in #63104).** The baseline gets much faster with an FP8 cache: its 48K prefill takes 1.89 s instead of 2.60 s with BF16, trtllm-gen in both cases. This path stays near 1.72 s because it computes in BF16. A native FP8 grouped kernel, as in #48726, would keep FP8's advantage. - **Memory.** The workspace is `max_model_len x 1,152 B` (75 MB at 64K). The dequantized query is a temporary of `tokens x heads x 1,152 B` per request, the same size as the head-major query copy of #63104's BF16 path. - **Query precision.** Grouped rows use the FP8 query the layer already produced for trtllm-gen, dequantized. Keeping a BF16 query for them would need the layer to quantize only the rows trtllm-gen reads. AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change, its tests and the benchmarks, which ran on my machine; I reviewed every changed line.
